The '''1752 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 21st edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[United Delet]] across [[New Ayre]] from 6 June to 6 July 1752, and was won by [[Praesyu]], who defeated [[Verusa]] 1–1 ''(5–4 pens)'' in the final at the Estadio Mantraal in [[Mantraal]] to claim their second FLLA World Cup title. Thirty-two nations qualified for the final tournament, drawn from the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]], and contested 64 matches across ten host venues.

The 1752 edition returned the FLLA World Cup to [[New Ayre]] for the first time since the [[1708 FLLA World Cup|1708 tournament]], hosted again by [[United Delet]]. The competition is remembered for the tactical sophistication of the leading sides and for one of the most tightly contested finals in the tournament's history: [[Praesyu]] and [[Verusa]] played to a 1–1 draw across normal time and extra time before Praesyu prevailed 5–4 in the resulting penalty shoot-out to claim their second FLLA World Cup title. The hosts [[United Delet]] reached the semi-finals in front of home crowds before losing 2–1 to [[Verusa]] after extra time at the Vairana Arena, recovering to take third place by beating the defending champions [[New Misos]] 2–1 at the Solekhan Memorial Stadium.

A total of 118 goals were scored in 64 matches at an average of 1.84 per match, the lowest goal-per-match average recorded at any FLLA World Cup since the [[1720 FLLA World Cup|1720 edition]]. The leading individual goalscorer was [[Verusa|Verusan]] forward Tovan Brunscar with 8 personal strikes, the highest individual tally at any FLLA World Cup since the [[1736 FLLA World Cup|1736 edition]]; Brunscar received the FLLA Marskval despite finishing on the losing side in the final. The FLLA Vairan Ball, awarded to the tournament's best player, was given to [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] central midfielder and captain Velim Khastane.

==Host selection==
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup bids}}

The [[NAFVL]]-backed bid from [[United Delet]] was confirmed as host of the 1752 FLLA World Cup by the [[FLLA]] Council on 14 February 1748, ending a bidding process that had opened twenty-two months earlier. The single-nation bid, formally submitted in October 1747 under the umbrella of the United Delet Arraby Federation, prevailed over rival proposals from [[Praesyu]], [[Lycroa]] and a joint [[Iainoa]]–[[Walporein]] bid coordinated by the [[NAFVL]] secretariat at the longlist stage. An earlier bid from [[Easuhura]] had been withdrawn in March 1747 after the AYFVL Council declined to advance two separate Ayuman submissions into the longlist round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/news/1748/host-selection-united-delet|title=United Delet confirmed as 1752 FLLA World Cup hosts|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 February 1748}}</ref>

The [[NAFVL]] case for the United Delet bid rested principally on the forty-four year gap since the [[1708 FLLA World Cup|1708 tournament]], the previous and only prior FLLA World Cup staged in [[New Ayre]], which had also been hosted by [[United Delet]]. The FLLA Council's published reasoning for awarding the 1752 tournament to United Delet cited the strength of the bid's stadium programme, the geographic balance argument from the [[NAFVL]], and the absence of a major continental tournament in [[New Ayre]] in the intervening four decades. The total infrastructure budget pledged by the United Delet federal government and the participating municipalities was {{lahn}}1.21&nbsp;billion, of which {{lahn}}340&nbsp;million was directed towards transport upgrades, principally the Mantraal–Khaldari express rail corridor and arterial road improvements connecting the ten host cities. A separate operational budget of {{lahn}}195&nbsp;million was allocated to security, broadcasting infrastructure and the volunteer programme.

==Participating teams and officials==

===Qualification===
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup qualification}}

A total of 32 places at the tournament were allocated across the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]]. Each confederation administered its own qualifying competition, with the format reflecting the size of its membership and its allocation of finals berths. The host association [[United Delet]] qualified as of right under FLLA hosting regulations and additionally took part in the [[NAFVL]] qualifying tournament in a non-binding capacity; United Delet were placed in the [[NAFVL]] central qualifying pool but withdrew from the qualifying matchday programme after the third round. The defending champions [[New Misos]], winners of the [[1748 FLLA World Cup]], qualified through the [[ATFVL]] qualifiers on merit.

The qualifying tournaments are summarised below; full results are recorded on the individual confederation pages.

===Final draw===
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup seeding}}

The final draw for the group stage was held at the United Delet Federal Convention Centre in [[Mantraal]] on 1 December 1751, six months before the opening match. The 32 qualified teams were divided into four pots of eight on the basis of their pre-tournament [[FLLA]] rankings, with the host [[United Delet]] and the seven highest-ranked sides ([[Praesyu]], [[New Misos]], [[Verusa]], [[Raledria]], [[Quidic]], [[Erkizil]] and [[Wundry]]) placed in the seeded pot. The three remaining pots were arranged on geographical lines so as to maximise the continental diversity of each group; under the procedure approved by the FLLA Organising Committee in September 1751, no group was permitted to contain more than two sides from any one confederation other than the host [[NAFVL]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1752/final-draw|title=Procedures for the 1752 FLLA World Cup final draw|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=10 September 1751}}</ref>

The draw was conducted by FLLA general secretary Maren Vossal and presented by United Delet broadcaster Renal Tavri, with retired internationals from each of the seven confederations drawing the team names. The ceremony was televised by 28 broadcasters across more than 110 countries.

===Officials===
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup officials}}

The FLLA Referees Committee appointed 22 refereeing trios, each consisting of one referee and two assistants from the same national association, and four support pairs drawn from a combined pool of 18 nations. The selections were announced in two tranches between September 1751 and February 1752, following an assessment programme at the [[1751 FLLA Continental Champions Cup]] and at senior friendlies organised across the ten host cities.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1752/officials-announced|title=Match officials confirmed for the 1752 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 February 1752}}</ref>

The opening match was refereed by Halric Ostley of [[Emara]], an [[AYFVL]]-affiliated official drafted into the appointment after the original nominee withdrew through injury in May 1752. The final was officiated by Jorgan Velendar of [[Quidic]] ([[QUFVL]]), the first Quidican referee to take charge of an FLLA World Cup final. The two semi-finals were taken by Min-Jun Park of [[Ashain]] ([[ATFVL]] support pair) for the first semi-final and Aelfric Holloway of [[Ealdorii]] ([[ATFVL]]) for the second. The 22 selected referees were drawn from 18 nations and represented all seven [[FLLA]] confederations.

==Squads==
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup squads}}

Each participating squad consisted of 22 players, two of whom were required to be goalkeepers, under the squad allocation in force since the [[1740 FLLA World Cup|1740 edition]]. Each participating national association was required to confirm its final 22-player squad with the FLLA no later than seven days before the opening match; late replacements were permitted in the event of serious injury at any time up to 24 hours before a team's first fixture. A total of 704 players were registered for the tournament, of whom 64 were goalkeepers.

The oldest player at the tournament was [[Raledria|Raledrian]] central defender Maric Helven, who was 38 years and 92 days old at the start of the competition; the youngest was [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] forward Alaric Sumar (19 years and 207 days), who would go on to win the [[#Awards|Best Young Player]] award. The mean age of registered players across the tournament was 26.7 years.

The squad nominally registered as the oldest by mean age was the [[Verusa|Verusan]] selection (28.4 years), with five outfield players above the age of 31 at registration; the youngest squad by mean age was the [[Erkizil|Erkizili]] selection (24.6 years), eight of whose 22 players were earning their first senior tournament call-ups. Three players at the tournament — [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] central midfielder Velim Khastane, [[New Misos|New Misosan]] goalkeeper Halen Dorvic and [[Raledria|Raledrian]] central defender Maric Helven — were appearing at their fourth FLLA World Cup, equalling the all-tournament record for repeat appearances at the time, set at the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]] by the [[Lycroa|Lycroan]] central midfielder Cario Velarzo. Khastane and Dorvic both captained their sides throughout the tournament; Helven was the [[Raledria|Raledrian]] vice-captain. The leading individual appearance maker of the tournament was [[United Delet|United Deletan]] right-back Halor Mendric, who played all seven of his country's matches in their entirety for a total of 690 minutes on the pitch.

A total of nineteen players withdrew between the publication of preliminary squads in May 1752 and the FLLA's deadline of 30 May 1752, fourteen on grounds of injury and five for personal or domestic reasons. The most senior late withdrawal was [[Verusa|Verusan]] central midfielder Kralan Voskari, who suffered a calf strain in a pre-tournament friendly on 26 May and was replaced by the uncapped 22-year-old Tobi Lehrek, who went on to score the third Verusan penalty of the [[#Final|final]] shoot-out. Two players who appeared in their country's [[1748 FLLA World Cup|1748]] final, [[New Misos|New Misosan]] forwards Veren Galenas and Imrad Solenchar, also withdrew through injury; both formally retired from international football before the [[1756 FLLA World Cup|1756 edition]].

==Venues==
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup venues}}

Ten stadiums in ten host cities were used in the final tournament, all located in [[United Delet]]. Four of the ten venues had been built specifically for the tournament or substantially redeveloped during the bidding period; the remaining six were existing top-flight venues that received targeted upgrades to seating and broadcasting facilities under FLLA Council resolution 1748/9. The ten-venue programme was the largest single-host stadium plan in the competition's history at the time, surpassing the seven-venue programme used at the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]].

The opening match was held at the Khaldari National Stadium in [[Khaldari]], the second-largest stadium in the host country, which also staged the second of two quarter-finals on 1 July. The final was held at the Estadio Mantraal in [[Mantraal]], a purpose-built venue of 80,000 seats inaugurated in February 1752. The two semi-finals were divided between the Talanvi Olympic Stadium in [[Talanvi]] and the Vairana Arena in [[Vairana]]. The third-place playoff was held at the Solekhan Memorial Stadium in [[Solekhan]].

===Venue profiles===

The '''Estadio Mantraal''', in [[Mantraal]], was the largest venue at the tournament and the principal final venue. The stadium, designed by the architectural studio Vohra Tasvil and inaugurated by the head of state of [[United Delet]] on 14 February 1752, was constructed on the site of the older Mantraal Federal Ground (closed 1748) on the eastern bank of the [[Mantraal]] river. The 80,000-seat ground hosted the [[#Final|final]], the second of the two [[#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]], the first of the [[#Round of 16|round-of-sixteen]] ties between [[Praesyu]] and [[Iainoa]], and three group-stage fixtures. The ground was the home stadium of the Praesyuan domestic-league club Mantraal Olympic from August 1752, having been transferred from federal to municipal ownership under the bid agreement of 1747.

The '''Khaldari National Stadium''' in [[Khaldari]] was the second-largest venue at the tournament with a redeveloped capacity of 75,000 and the principal northern-host venue. The ground, originally opened in 1701 and extensively redeveloped between 1749 and 1752 to bring it within FLLA capacity guidance for opening fixtures, hosted the opening match between [[United Delet]] and [[Trian]] on 6 June, the first of the two [[#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] on 29 June, the [[#Round of 16|round-of-sixteen]] tie between [[New Misos]] and [[Ukhdari]], and three group-stage fixtures.

The '''Talanvi Olympic Stadium''' in [[Talanvi]], a 72,000-seat stadium opened for the [[1738 Talanvi Summer Games]] and the regular home venue of the [[United Delet]] national side, hosted the first of the two [[#Semi-finals|semi-finals]] between [[Praesyu]] and [[New Misos]] on 3 July, one [[#Round of 16|round-of-sixteen]] tie, and three group-stage fixtures. The '''Vairana Arena''' in [[Vairana]], a 68,000-seat venue opened in March 1752 specifically for the tournament, hosted the second [[#Semi-finals|semi-final]] between [[United Delet]] and [[Verusa]], one [[#Round of 16|round-of-sixteen]] tie, and three group-stage fixtures.

The '''Solekhan Memorial Stadium''' in [[Solekhan]], a 60,000-seat venue completed in 1738 in commemoration of the [[United Delet]] federation's centenary, hosted the [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] between [[United Delet]] and [[New Misos]] on 5 July, alongside one [[#Round of 16|round-of-sixteen]] tie and three group-stage fixtures. The remaining five venues — the Calhantri Federal Stadium, the Mordeli City Stadium, the Zarnath Coliseum, the Lurimah Field and the Ravohni Sports Park — were used principally for group-stage fixtures, with five between them also staging individual knockout-stage ties.

===Team base camps===

Each of the 32 participating squads selected a base camp from a shortlist of 64 candidate sites circulated by the United Delet Arraby Federation in October 1751. Most teams opted for camps in or around the larger host cities, with eight squads basing themselves within a one-hour radius of [[Mantraal]], six near [[Khaldari]] and five each in or around [[Talanvi]] and [[Vairana]]. The remaining eight were divided between the smaller host cities and the inland highland corridor between [[Solekhan]] and [[Calhantri]], which became known during the tournament as the "Lokani belt".

==Innovations==

The 1752 FLLA World Cup introduced a number of regulatory and presentational changes. The competition was the first FLLA World Cup at which the FLLA Marskval, the FLLA Bastion and the FLLA Best Young Player Award were formally constituted as standing tournament awards under FLLA Council resolution 1751/7, having previously been issued on an ad-hoc basis at the discretion of the FLLA Awards Committee. The standing-award framework was retained at the [[1756 FLLA World Cup|1756 edition]] and at every subsequent FLLA World Cup. The 1752 tournament was also the first to use a single round of seeding pots organised on the basis of the published [[FLLA]] world rankings rather than continental rankings, a change adopted by the FLLA Council on 4 October 1751 to address concerns that the previous draw procedure had over-weighted hemispheric balance at the expense of competitive parity. A third procedural change, the introduction of a four-official refereeing trio with a designated fourth official at the touchline, was incorporated at the request of the [[NAFVL]] in November 1751 and would be retained without amendment at the [[1756 FLLA World Cup|1756 edition]].

==Format==

The 32 qualified teams were divided into eight groups of four for the group stage, drawn at the [[#Final draw|final draw]] on 1 December 1751. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing three matches; teams were awarded three points for a win, one for a draw and none for a defeat. The top two teams from each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]] while the bottom two were eliminated. Tiebreakers between teams level on points were applied in the following order: overall goal difference, overall goals scored, head-to-head record, fair-play points, and, if necessary, a drawing of lots by the FLLA Organising Committee.

In the knockout stage, fixtures were single-elimination ties played over 90 minutes; ties level at the end of normal time were extended by a single 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]] of two 15-minute halves, with a [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] used to decide ties that remained level after extra time. Both semi-final losers contested a [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] on 5 July 1752.

==Opening ceremony==

The opening ceremony of the 1752 FLLA World Cup was held at the Khaldari National Stadium on 6 June 1752, sixty minutes before the kick-off of the opening match between [[United Delet]] and [[Trian]]. Directed by United Delet stage producer Lerin Vohra and choreographed by Esma Daltri, the ceremony lasted 28 minutes and featured 920 dancers, 180 musicians and a massed entrance representing each of the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]]. The performance opened with a sequence depicting the historical migration routes of [[New Ayre]] across its eastern coastal plain, before transitioning to a portrayal of the seven confederations arrayed as a single concentric ring around the centre circle. The United Delet vocalist Inara Mohran, joined by the Khaldari Choral Society, performed the tournament's official theme song "One Crossing" as the closing item of the ceremony.

Attending dignitaries included the head of state of [[United Delet]], the President of the FLLA Council, the heads of state of [[Praesyu]], [[New Misos]] and [[Verusa]], and 74 ambassadors and senior diplomatic representatives. The ceremony was watched by an estimated worldwide television audience of 2.1 billion people.

==Group stage==

The 32 qualified teams were drawn into eight groups of four. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing three matches; the top two finishers in each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]] while the bottom two were eliminated. Group rankings were settled first on points (three for a win, one for a draw), then on goal difference and goals scored.

The group stage produced one perfect record: [[Erkizil]] in Group F took maximum points from their three matches, the only side at the tournament to come through the group phase with both a perfect points record and a positive goal difference of four or more. The biggest single-match upset of the round was the 1–0 victory for [[Sivoso]] over [[Verusa]] at the Calhantri Federal Stadium on 7 June, the first defeat suffered by a seeded side at the tournament; despite the result, [[Verusa]] recovered to win Group E and advanced through the knockout stages to the final. Defending champions [[New Misos]] survived a tightly contested Group D on goal difference, finishing level on points with [[Andsaudare]] and advancing as group winners by a margin of one goal.

All times listed are United Delet Time ([[wikipedia:UTC+05:00|UDT]], [[wikipedia:UTC|UTC]]+5).

==Knockout stage==

The knockout stage involved the sixteen teams that advanced from the group stage. Matches still level after 90 minutes were extended by a 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]]; if scores remained tied after extra time, the tie was decided by [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Three of the eight round-of-sixteen ties and two of the four quarter-finals required additional time, and three ties in total were decided on penalties, including the [[#Final|final]] itself. The cumulative goal total of 35 across the sixteen knockout matches was the lowest at any FLLA World Cup since the [[1720 FLLA World Cup|1720 edition]] and was widely cited at the time as evidence of the tactical caution that came to define the tournament.

===Round of 16===

The eight group winners were drawn against the eight group runners-up, with each match-up pairing teams from different groups. Three of the eight ties required additional time, and one was decided on penalties. The highest-scoring fixture of the round was [[Praesyu]] 3–0 [[Iainoa]] at the Estadio Mantraal, in which Praesyuan forward Alaric Sumar scored his first two FLLA World Cup goals; the lowest-scoring decisive fixture was the host nation's 2–1 victory over [[Ztesh]] at the Zarnath Coliseum, settled in the 109th minute by United Delet substitute Marek Calahn after the Ztesh midfielder Kashik Tonaq had cancelled out an opening goal by Renal Reka.

===Quarter-finals===

The four quarter-finals produced two ties decided in normal time and two requiring additional time, with one resolved on penalties. [[Praesyu]] beat [[Quidic]] 2–1 in extra time at the Estadio Mantraal, advancing through a 113th-minute winner by captain Velim Khastane that drew sustained acclaim from the [[Mantraal]] crowd. [[New Misos]] beat [[Raledria]] 1–0 at the Khaldari National Stadium through a single goal by Sebrek Galenas in the 56th minute, retaining their tournament unbeaten run from the group stage. [[Verusa]] beat [[Wundry]] 1–0 at the Lurimah Field, with the only goal of the match scored by Tovan Brunscar from a tight angle in the 38th minute; the result extended Brunscar's individual tally for the tournament to five goals. The hosts [[United Delet]] beat [[Erkizil]] 4–3 on penalties after a 1–1 draw at the Ravohni Sports Park, advancing to the semi-finals via a decisive shoot-out save by goalkeeper Solan Mahiri.

===Semi-finals===

The first semi-final at the Talanvi Olympic Stadium was decided inside 90 minutes by a single goal: [[Praesyu]] beat the defending champions [[New Misos]] 1–0 through a 62nd-minute strike from captain Velim Khastane, who collected a low cross from Alaric Sumar and turned in his third goal of the tournament. The result eliminated [[New Misos]] one round before the final and gave Praesyu their first FLLA World Cup final appearance since the [[1740 FLLA World Cup|1740 edition]]. The second semi-final at the Vairana Arena required extra time; the hosts [[United Delet]] and [[Verusa]] were level at 1–1 after 90 minutes before Verusan forward Tovan Brunscar scored from a close-range header in the 104th minute to seal a 2–1 win, ending the host nation's tournament in front of a 67,300 crowd.

===Third place playoff===

The third-place playoff was contested between the two losing semi-finalists at the Solekhan Memorial Stadium on 5 July. The hosts [[United Delet]] beat the defending champions [[New Misos]] 2–1 to take third place at the tournament, with goals from Renal Reka and Marek Calahn either side of a New Misos equaliser by Sebrek Galenas. The result gave [[United Delet]] their highest finish at an FLLA World Cup since the [[1708 FLLA World Cup|1708 edition]], which they had won as hosts, and confirmed [[New Misos]] as defending champions finishing fourth at the subsequent tournament for the second consecutive cycle, after the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]] in which they had also finished fourth in defence of their [[1740 FLLA World Cup|1740 title]].

===Final===
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup final}}

The final was contested between [[Praesyu]] and [[Verusa]], the Group A and Group E winners respectively, on 6 July 1752 at the Estadio Mantraal in [[Mantraal]] in front of an attendance of 79,800. [[Praesyu]] entered the match having conceded only two goals across their six previous fixtures, while [[Verusa]] had reached the final with the tournament's leading goalscorer Tovan Brunscar in the form of his career. The match opened with Verusa taking the lead in the 23rd minute through Brunscar, who turned in a low cross from right winger Halo Markenrick from inside the six-yard box for his eighth goal of the tournament. [[Praesyu]] equalised in the 47th minute through Alaric Sumar, who advanced onto a deflected Khastane pass in the inside-left channel and struck a low shot past Verusan goalkeeper Aksen Lerendar.

The match remained at 1–1 through the remainder of normal time and through the two halves of extra time, with both sides defending in increasingly compact shapes and producing only a single shot on target between them across the 30-minute additional period. The tie was decided by a penalty shoot-out, the first FLLA World Cup final in the competition's history to be settled in this way. Praesyu won the shoot-out 5–4 after Verusan defender Reinhold Kasspar struck the crossbar with the seventh kick of the sequence and the Praesyuan substitute Donaldi Vellan converted the decisive tenth. The win gave [[Praesyu]] their second FLLA World Cup title.

[[Praesyu]] and the hosts [[United Delet]] finished as the tournament's joint leading scoring nations with 11 goals each across seven matches, ahead of runners-up [[Verusa]] (10 in seven). The overall goal-per-match average of 1.84 was the lowest at any FLLA World Cup since the [[1720 FLLA World Cup|1720 edition]] and prompted the FLLA Tactical Review Committee, in a report published in October 1752, to attribute the figure to the widespread adoption of compact mid-block defensive systems among the leading sides.

===Discipline===

The FLLA Disciplinary Committee issued a total of 196 yellow cards and 11 red cards across the 64 matches of the tournament, an average of 3.06 yellows and 0.17 reds per match. The most-cautioned team was [[Verusa]], with 14 yellow cards and 1 red across their seven matches; [[Iainoa]] received the fewest among the teams reaching the round of sixteen, with three yellows and no reds across their four matches, helping the team win the [[#Awards|FLLA Fair Play Trophy]]. Four players received red cards in the knockout stage: one in the round of sixteen, two in the quarter-finals and one in the semi-final between [[United Delet]] and [[Verusa]].

==Awards==

The Best Player award, formally titled the FLLA Vairan Ball, was awarded by a panel of seven sports journalists drawn from each of the seven confederations to [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] central midfielder and captain Velim Khastane, who contributed three goals and six assists across the seven matches of the champions' run to the title. Khastane was the first Praesyuan player to win the award since [[1736 FLLA World Cup|1736]]. Tovan Brunscar of [[Verusa]] took the Marskval with eight personal strikes, the first finalist player to win the individual scoring award at any FLLA World Cup; the FLLA Awards Committee noted in its final report that Brunscar's tally accounted for approximately seven per cent of the entire tournament's goal output.

The Bastion, awarded to the tournament's best goalkeeper, went to Praesyuan goalkeeper Donval Ireshi, who conceded just three goals across his country's seven matches and kept clean sheets in the round of sixteen, the semi-final and the third hour of the final's normal-and-extra-time period. Praesyuan forward Alaric Sumar, 19 years old at the start of the tournament, was named Best Young Player after starting all seven of [[Praesyu]]'s matches and scoring four goals, including the equaliser in the final. [[Iainoa]] received the Fair Play award after finishing the tournament with the fewest disciplinary points of any of the sixteen knockout-stage participants.

==Preparations and costs==

The total budget allocated to the 1752 FLLA World Cup by the United Delet Arraby Federation and the federal government of [[United Delet]] was {{lahn}}1.41&nbsp;billion. Of this, {{lahn}}875&nbsp;million was directed towards stadium construction and renovation across the ten venues, {{lahn}}340&nbsp;million towards transport upgrades (principally the Mantraal–Khaldari express rail corridor and arterial road improvements connecting the ten host cities), and {{lahn}}195&nbsp;million towards operational expenditure including security, broadcasting infrastructure and the volunteer programme. Per-venue capital costs averaged {{lahn}}87&nbsp;million across the ten stadiums, a figure later cited by FLLA reviewers as broadly in line with comparable single-host editions despite the unusually large number of venues.

Four of the ten venues, comprising the Estadio Mantraal, the Vairana Arena, the Lurimah Field and the Ravohni Sports Park, were either newly built or extensively redeveloped for the tournament. The newest, Estadio Mantraal, was inaugurated on 14 February 1752, four months before the opening match. Total stadium construction overran the original budget by 11&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent, primarily because of cost escalation at the Estadio Mantraal and the Vairana Arena; the federal government absorbed the overrun under a guarantee provision agreed with the United Delet Arraby Federation at the bid stage in October 1747.

The combined security operation involved 28,000 police and military personnel deployed across the ten host cities, the largest such single-nation deployment in the competition's history at the time. No serious incidents were reported during the competition. A dedicated public transport extension programme, providing free local-network travel to ticket holders for the day of each match, was introduced for the duration of the tournament and was retained by several host municipalities as a permanent matchday provision following the closing ceremony.

Total tournament revenue, audited by the FLLA in August 1752, was {{lahn}}2.02&nbsp;billion, against costs of {{lahn}}1.41&nbsp;billion, yielding a net surplus of {{lahn}}610&nbsp;million. The FLLA's standard 18&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent host-association allocation returned {{lahn}}364&nbsp;million to the United Delet Arraby Federation, which was retained in full by the federation under the single-host allocation formula then in force.

==Marketing==
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup marketing}}

The marketing programme for the 1752 FLLA World Cup was overseen by the United Delet Arraby Federation in partnership with the FLLA's commercial division, with creative direction by the Mantraal-based studio Vohra Tasvil. The programme included the official emblem, mascot, match ball and theme song (see [[#Symbols|Symbols]] below), a domestic travelling-trophy tour that visited 34 cities across [[United Delet]] in the year preceding the tournament, and a tiered sponsorship structure of four worldwide partners, ten host-nation partners and six regional supporters. Total sponsorship revenue across all three tiers was {{lahn}}720&nbsp;million, the highest gross sponsorship figure recorded by any FLLA World Cup to date at the time of the tournament.

==Symbols==
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup symbols}}

===Emblem===

The official emblem of the tournament, designed by the Mantraal-based studio Vohra Tasvil, was unveiled on 6 June 1750 in a public ceremony at the United Delet Federal Convention Centre in [[Mantraal]]. The design depicts the silhouette of a single trophy rising from a stylised eastern coastal landscape, framed by seven radial bands representing the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]]. The radial-band motif was drawn from the cartography of the United Delet eastern seaboard and was intended to symbolise the host nation's reception of the global tournament. The emblem received the FLLA Council's formal endorsement in October 1750 after a four-week consultation period with the seven confederations.

===Mascot===

The official mascot of the 1752 FLLA World Cup, named '''Mahari''', is an anthropomorphic eastern-plains horse dressed in a green-and-blue panel jersey representing the national colours of [[United Delet]]. The mascot was selected by a domestic public vote organised by the United Delet Arraby Federation in the spring of 1750, with three candidate designs presented to voters across the host nation and in print; Mahari prevailed over a stylised river crane ("Velendi") and a coastal seabird ("Aksir") with 52&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent of the 2.7 million votes cast.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1750/mascot-vote|title=Mahari named official mascot of 1752 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[NAFVL]]|date=22 May 1750}}</ref>

===Match ball===

The official match ball, manufactured by the Mantraal-based sports equipment maker Lokani Sport, was branded the '''Marivat'''. The Marivat featured a 32-panel hand-stitched construction in a green-and-gold livery, a presentation chosen to evoke the eastern-plains motif of the tournament emblem. The ball was the last FLLA World Cup match ball to use the traditional 32-panel hand-stitched construction; from the [[1756 FLLA World Cup|1756 edition]] onwards, FLLA technical regulations permitted reduced-panel constructions. A distinct gold-coloured version of the ball, the Marivat Final, was used in the final, the third-place playoff and the two semi-finals.

===Permanent trophy===

The permanent trophy of the 1752 FLLA World Cup, presented to the winners alongside the rotating [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]] at the closing ceremony of the [[#Final|final]], was the '''Vairana''', a 42-centimetre patinated bronze sculpture commissioned by the United Delet Arraby Federation from the Mantraal-based studio Vohra Tasvil, the same studio responsible for the [[#Emblem|tournament emblem]]. The work depicts a stylised eastern-coastal landscape in low relief, the central figure of which is a single rising column representing the column of the Vairana Arena where the second [[#Semi-finals|semi-final]] was contested; the studio's principal sculptor Lerin Tasvil drew the name from the city of [[Vairana]] at the request of the federation. Cast at the federation's Mantraal foundry in March 1752, the Vairana was unveiled on 4 April 1752, ten weeks before the opening match. Following [[Praesyu]]'s [[#Final|1–1 (5–4 pens) win]] over [[Verusa]], the trophy was transferred to permanent retention by the [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] federation and is displayed at the Brimasha Federal Gallery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1752/permanent-trophy|title=The Vairana unveiled as 1752 FLLA World Cup permanent trophy|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=4 April 1752}}</ref>

===Theme song===

The official theme song of the tournament, "One Crossing", was composed by United Delet musician Talen Vohra with lyrics jointly written by Vohra and the vocalist Inara Mohran, who also performed the track. The studio recording was released on 9 March 1752 and topped the United Delet domestic charts across the months of April and May 1752, the first sports-themed track to lead the United Delet charts since the [[1748 FLLA World Cup|1748 edition]].

==Media==
{{Main|1752 FLLA World Cup broadcasting rights}}

The 1752 FLLA World Cup was broadcast in 126 countries by 38 official television partners and a further 14 official radio partners. Domestic broadcasting rights in [[United Delet]] were held by the United Delet National Broadcaster (UDNB), which produced the host feed and screened all 64 matches across its terrestrial network. The international rights for the [[AYFVL]] region were held by the [[Verusa|Verusan]] public-service broadcaster VRT; the [[ATFVL]] rights by the [[New Misos|New Misosan]] National Network (NMNN); and the [[QUFVL]] rights by a three-broadcaster consortium led by the Quidican National Network (QNN).

The final between [[Praesyu]] and [[Verusa]] was the most-watched television broadcast in [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] history at the time, drawing a peak audience of 18.2 million viewers (representing approximately 71&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent of the active television audience in the country). Worldwide, the FLLA reported a cumulative live broadcast audience for the tournament of 2.1 billion individual viewers across all matches, with 980 million individuals tuning in to at least part of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1752/audience-summary|title=1752 FLLA World Cup viewership summary|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=10 August 1752}}</ref>

===Attendance===

Cumulative attendance across the 64 matches of the tournament was 2,948,000 spectators, an average of 46,063 per match. The highest single-match attendance was the 79,800 recorded at the [[#Final|final]] between [[Praesyu]] and [[Verusa]] at the Estadio Mantraal in [[Mantraal]], just below the stadium's listed all-seater capacity of 80,000; the lowest was the 36,400 attending the Group F fixture between [[Ucrua]] and [[Laselteh]] at the Calhantri Federal Stadium on 18 June.

Across the tournament, attendance averaged 54,300 in the knockout stage and 43,750 in the group stage. The three highest single-match attendances of the tournament were all recorded at the Estadio Mantraal, with the final, the QF1 between [[Praesyu]] and [[Quidic]], and the round-of-16 fixture between [[Praesyu]] and [[Iainoa]] all drawing crowds in excess of 78,000.

==Controversies==

The most prominent dispute of the tournament arose from the [[#Semi-finals|semi-final]] between [[United Delet]] and [[Verusa]] at the Vairana Arena on 3 July, in which the hosts' equalising goal in the 41st minute was scored from a position that the Verusan Arraby Association contended had been offside. Broadcast footage subsequently confirmed that United Delet forward Renal Reka had been narrowly onside at the moment the pass was played; the FLLA Disciplinary Committee declined to entertain the Verusan complaint on 4 July, citing the finality of on-field decisions under the laws of the game then in force, and the result of the match was undisturbed. The incident was later cited by the FLLA Refereeing Committee as a key motivation for the introduction of standardised electronic communications protocols at the [[1756 FLLA World Cup|1756 edition]].

A second incident, the dismissal of [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] central defender Karne Tovris in the 90th minute of the [[#Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] against [[Quidic]] for a second bookable offence, was widely cited at the time as a notable refereeing call: Tovris was the first defender of a tournament champion side to receive a red card at the quarter-final stage in three editions. Tovris was suspended from the [[#Semi-finals|semi-final]] against [[New Misos]] but returned to the starting eleven for the [[#Final|final]] and converted Praesyu's fourth shoot-out kick.

A third dispute, of an administrative rather than sporting character, arose from the ticketing programme for the opening match between [[United Delet]] and [[Trian]] at the Khaldari National Stadium on 6 June. Approximately 3,200 tickets allocated to the United Delet Arraby Federation's domestic-supporter pool were issued in error to overseas applicants through a software fault in the federation's online distribution platform; the affected tickets were honoured for entry on the day, but a compensation scheme covering the cost of travel and accommodation was instituted by the federation in July 1752 for 1,710 registered supporters who had been unable to obtain replacement tickets through the second-allocation round. The federation's then-commercial director, Tovis Rendari, resigned from his post in October 1752 following the publication of an internal audit of the distribution platform.

A fourth incident concerned the post-tournament doping case involving [[Andsaudare|Andsaudaran]] central midfielder Selvar Heskaran, who returned an adverse analytical finding for a stimulant during the routine post-match sample collected following his country's [[#Round of 16|round-of-sixteen]] loss to [[Quidic]] at the Khaldari National Stadium on 22 June. Heskaran was provisionally suspended by the FLLA Disciplinary Committee on 14 July 1752, pending the analysis of his B-sample; the B-sample analysis, conducted at the FLLA-accredited laboratory at [[Mantraal]] in August 1752, confirmed the finding and Heskaran received an eighteen-month competitive suspension on 9 September 1752, backdated to the date of the original test. The Andsaudaran Arraby Federation accepted the finding and did not appeal. The case was the first formally upheld doping finding arising from an FLLA World Cup since the [[1740 FLLA World Cup|1740 edition]].

==Aftermath==

[[Praesyu]]'s victory was their second FLLA World Cup title. The result was widely celebrated in [[Praesyu]], where the team's homecoming parade through central [[Brimasha]] on 9 July 1752 drew an estimated crowd of 3.4 million along a six-kilometre route from the Praesyuan federal palace to the National Assembly. As reigning champions, Praesyu qualified automatically for the [[1756 FLLA World Cup|subsequent 1756 edition]] under the FLLA's defending-champion exemption then in force; Praesyu were drawn into Group D at the 1756 tournament and were eliminated in the group stage, finishing third in the group behind [[Quidic]] and [[Taval]].

Across the host nation, the tournament was judged a substantial organisational success. An independent post-event report commissioned by the United Delet federal government and published in October 1752 estimated the net economic contribution to the host economy at {{lahn}}2.8&nbsp;billion, against gross public expenditure of {{lahn}}1.41&nbsp;billion across infrastructure and operations. International visitor arrivals across [[United Delet]] over the tournament period totalled 720,000, the highest cumulative tournament-period visitor figure recorded in [[New Ayre]] up to that date. The matchday public transport provision introduced for the tournament was retained on a permanent basis after the closing ceremony by the municipal authorities of [[Mantraal]], [[Khaldari]], [[Talanvi]] and [[Vairana]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nafvl.org/1752/post-event-economic-impact|title=1752 FLLA World Cup post-event economic impact report|publisher=[[NAFVL]]|date=8 October 1752}}</ref>

The next edition of the FLLA World Cup, the [[1756 FLLA World Cup]], was awarded to a four-nation [[QUFVL]] bid coordinated by [[Erkizil]], [[Quidic]], [[Wundry]] and [[Ztesh]] at the FLLA Council meeting of 7 March 1751, a year before the 1752 tournament began. The single-host stadium programme of ten venues used in 1752 was the largest such single-nation plan in the competition's history at the time and was retained as a procedural reference point in FLLA bidding guidance issued after the tournament; the four-nation hosting model that the [[QUFVL]] would introduce at the 1756 edition was a direct response to the absence of any comparable single-host capacity within the [[QUFVL]] member nations.
